checked_equations_and_outputs.steady_or_periodic_constant_probe: For x[n]=1, both have tap sum 1 and produce y[n]=1; a period-3 constant record gives [1,1,1] for both. The observation matrix has rank 1.
checked_equations_and_outputs.finite_zero_padded_constant_probe: For x=[1,1,1], full linear outputs are [1,1,1,0,0] and [0,1,1,1,0], so edge transients distinguish the kernels. In general y[0]=h0, y[1]=h0+h1, y[2]=h0+h1+h2 recovers a causal three-tap kernel.

checked_equations_and_outputs.general_condition: For a finite L-tap identification, the stacked convolution/design matrix of the observed probes must have column rank L. A second input is evidence only to the extent that it adds independent excitation.
checked_equations_and_outputs.claim_limit: Passing one held-out input supports the model on that input; it does not by itself prove global LTI behavior or uniqueness under noise/model mismatch.

issues.detail: course.yaml promises one three-tap hand convolution and the brief calls for a three-tap echo, but every specified numeric hand example uses h=[1,-1] or h=[1,0.5], both two-tap kernels. The exercise-fix packet also calls h=[1,-1] the same three-tap kernel. No three coefficients, sparse delay indices, or sample rate are supplied.

The claim that one constant input cannot uniquely identify a kernel is not true for the full output of a finite zero-padded causal experiment, whose startup edge equations can recover the taps. State periodic/eternal constant input, steady-state-only scoring, circular convolution, or an explicit crop that removes edge transients.

Normalized output error has no declared norm or zero-output rule, and second-input validation has no excitation/rank requirement. Define the metric and use an impulse or another probe whose stacked convolution matrix has rank three.

The brief routes LTI tests, impulse responses, and convolution to MIT 6.003 Sessions 1-3 and Problem Sets 1-2. The local course corpus places the relevant first treatment in Session 8 slides 15-48 and the worked convolution set in Problem Set 5; Sessions 1-3 instead emphasize abstraction, difference equations, feedback, and modes.

Oppenheim Chapter 2 §§2.2-2.4 support system tests and the LTI convolution derivation, but the standalone identity x[n]=sum_m x[m]delta[n-m] is introduced in §2.1.1. Add §2.1.1 when citing every-sequence impulse decomposition.
The brief cites Orfanidis Chapter 4 §§4.1-4.4 for methods, but §4.4 is the problem set. Exact method provenance is §§4.1.1-4.1.10 and §§4.3.1-4.3.4; the LTI derivation itself is Chapter 3 §§3.2-3.3.

The notation ledger and brief require dummy m, while course.yaml and concepts.yaml display sum_k x[k]h[n-k]. The lesson should use m and treat the schema forms as expressions requiring notation translation, not as the production notation.
